evidence_summary: Primary studies support IL-21 signaling through the IL21R/common-gamma receptor complex with JAK1/JAK3 and STAT3 activation, and show IL-21-induced IL2RA/CD25 expression in human naive B cells. STAT3 loss and IL21R or IL2RG deficiency impair the IL2RA response; chromatin immunoprecipitation supports IL2RA as a direct STAT3 target.
limitations: The receptor-proximal JAK1/JAK3 relay is source-supported, but the current graph has no direct JAK1/JAK3-to-STAT3 edge and no bare-STAT3-to-IL2RA edge. Preserve the human B-cell and receptor-reconstituted contexts; do not infer SCI receiver-cell activity or a universal IL-21 response.

citation_note: Primary IL-21 receptor/STAT3 and MYC studies: PMID:17234735; PMID:19965678.
evidence_summary: Primary studies show that IL-21 receptor signaling activates STAT3 through the common-gamma receptor system and that IL-21-activated STAT3 upregulates c-MYC in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma cells, with downstream cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis. The IL21R cytoplasmic Y510/JAK-STAT competence study supports the receptor-proximal signaling context.
limitations: The MYC result is demonstrated in human lymphoma cell lines and primary tumors rather than SCI receiver cells. Preserve the STAT3-to-MYC evidence and do not generalize the apoptotic output or infer a universal IL-21 phenotype.
